packages.summary:
Each stone's photo colour is now stored with the mosaic, and the photo-to-stone deviation can be recomputed at any time against the stone's current colour. For an unedited mosaic the result is exactly the compute's own numbers (mean, max, p95 and per-colour ΔE), not just within rounding. There is no UI yet, so the user sees nothing new until wave 6 builds the deviation map on top of this.

**What was built**
- `types.ts`: `MosaicData.targets?: PhotoTargets` and the wave-6 contract field `Material.colorSource`, exactly as specified.
- `mosaic.ts`: `computeMosaic` fills the targets from the values it already measured; the result itself is unchanged and the golden fixture is untouched.
- `serialize.ts`: pack/unpack, worker transfer and `cloneMosaic` carry the targets. Stored fields are `tKind`, `tLab1`, `tLab2`, `tLine`, `tSubLen`, `tSubLab`, all `Uint8Array`, so the project file carries them without a format change. Older or inconsistent data loads without targets.
- `deviation.ts` (new): `deviationForPiece`, `deviationForCell`, `deviationMap`, `topDeviations` (optional range), `deviationSummary`, `deviationByColor`, `nearestColorForPiece`, `pieceTarget`, `targetState`, `hasPhotoTargets`, `DEVIATION_LEGEND`/`deviationBin`.
- Stones without a photo reference return null/NaN with a reason, never an estimate: freeform (`free`), shape changed since compute (`shape`), grid computed before this feature (`legacy`). Undo, or choosing the same shape again, makes the reference valid again.

**The interrupted draft (5066762)** applied cleanly; I kept its structure and reworked it. The main changes:
- k×k sub-stone targets are stored unrounded (Float32) instead of quantised, which is what makes the results exact.
- Cut lines are compared exactly instead of with a tolerance.
- Targets that are inconsistent in memory are ignored, not trusted.
- `cloneMosaic` is a real deep copy again.
- Added `deviationByColor` and p95; dropped a duplicate of the existing `computedDeltaE` helper.

**Measured**
- Storage: 4 bytes per cell + 15 per two-part cell + (1 + 12·k²) per k×k cell. Portrait sample: 5.05 bytes per cell.
- 2M cells in the browser: the mosaic record in IndexedDB is 19.1 MB, of which 7.7 MB are targets (11.5 MB without). Saving after an edit took 0.5 s.
- `deviationMap` at 2M cells: about 50 ms in Node on the smooth upscaled sample; about 600 ms when no colour pair repeats. Portrait sample: 1–2 ms.
packages.notes:
**Deviations from the briefing**
1. In memory the targets are one object, `MosaicData.targets?: PhotoTargets` (kind, lab1, lab2, line, subLen, subLab), not three loose fields with a Map. The stored fields keep the briefing's names plus `tKind`, `tLine` and `tSubLen`. Reason: a target only belongs to the shape it was measured for, so the compute-time shape must be stored to detect manual shape changes honestly.
2. k×k sub-stone targets are stored as Float32 (12 bytes per sub-stone) instead of quantised (3 bytes). The compute measures sub-stones against unrounded values, and quantising could shift a single ΔE by up to about 0.9. With Float32 the deviation of an unedited grid is exactly the compute's result. Whole stones and two-part cells are already measured on the 3-byte grid, so they stay at 3 bytes.
3. `packMosaic(d, { targets: false })` exists but nothing calls it yet. It is meant for the stats, PDF and CSV worker requests in useProject.ts, StepPdf.tsx and StepPlan.tsx, which are not my files. At 2M cells the extra copy was not measurable in Node (about 12 ms either way), so I did not make an out-of-ownership edit for it.

**Out-of-ownership edit**
- `src/core/materialsCsv.ts`, types only: new `CsvMaterialField = Exclude<keyof Material, 'colorSource'>`, used in seven declarations. Without it the mandatory contract field breaks typecheck in materialsCsv.ts and Materials.tsx. No runtime change; Materials.tsx is untouched.

**Not done, or still open**
- No UI: the user cannot see the deviation yet. w6-compare-batch builds the map and list. The stone-inspector line "Fotofarbe vs. Steinfarbe, ΔE, bessere Farbe" from the corrected proposal is in no wave-6 package's ownership (StoneDialog.tsx); `pieceTarget`, `deviationForPiece` and `nearestColorForPiece` are ready for it.
- The targets live inside the mosaic record, so they are rewritten on every mosaic save (+4 bytes per cell; 19.1 MB instead of 11.5 MB at 2M cells). A separate record written once per compute would avoid that, but needs db.ts and useProject.ts.
- The project file grows by about 5.3 characters per cell.
- The colours table in step 5 still shows compute-time `matchDeltaE` and hides it after edits; `deviationByColor` could give a live value there (StepColors.tsx is not mine).
- `Material.colorSource` is the contract only: no CSV column yet, and project import passes it through unvalidated. Both belong to w6-colour-measure.
- Float32 bytes are stored in platform byte order, the same assumption the existing `lineVal` field in the project file already makes.

**For wave 6**
- w6-compare-batch: pass the compute's formula, `computedDeltaE(rec.computedWith)` from staleReasons.ts, not the current setting. NaN in the map means no reference; `targetState(data, idx)` and `summary.missing` give the reason. After a single edit, `deviationForCell(idx)` is enough.
- w6-fine-tiles: forced SUB cells need no change here. If it changes how sub-stone colours are measured, the exactness tests in tests/w5-target-colours.test.ts will show it.

**For w7 (README)**
- Photo colour per stone is stored with the grid, about 4 bytes per cell.
- Projects computed before this version have no per-stone deviation until they are recomputed.

**Verification extras**
- A mutation probe with 10 deliberate bugs (rank tracking, wrong target, cut-line check, length checks, cache key, rounding, shape detection, packing, tie order) was run against the new unit tests; all 10 were caught. The first run missed two: one was a real gap (cache key), now covered by a dedicated test, and the other showed a redundant comparison, which I simplified.
- The e2e bundles the deviation core with esbuild into the page and computes on what the app really stored. It covers both commit paths: adopting the live preview and a fresh worker compute.
- The preview server on 4300 is stopped. The node_modules symlink and dist are ignored and not committed. No dependencies added, no i18n keys, no CSS.
- e2e output is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/wave5/w5-target-colours/ (e2e, e2e-own, e2e-own-gross, plus logs of the eight related suites).

packages.summary:
Step 10 now says before export how many pages the PDF will have, broken down per part, and that number matched the generated PDF in every case tested (e.g. portrait sample: "ca. 49 Seiten", PDF 49 pages). Large exports are offered in parts instead of crashing, sections can always be chosen, and stale or mismatched data needs an explicit confirm.

**Page estimate**
- The page plan is measured in advance in the worker by a dry run of the PDF generator (new request `pdfPlan`, about 0.3–0.5 s for the samples, 1.1 s for 314k cells in Node). `planPdfPages` with these measurements gives the total.
- The "Inhalt" list follows the toggles: excluded items are struck through with the reason, and each item shows its pages. While measuring, only the certain numbers (laying sheets) are shown.
- Every number before export carries "ca."; the "many pages" warning uses the total.
- The fit option shows the real scale ("An Seite anpassen (1:1,25)"). New selectors: Codeplan automatisch/immer/aus, and Koordinaten kompakt/je Stein (the limit field now only appears for "Je Stein").

**Section selection (new `SectionPicker.tsx`)**
- The sections are laid out as in the mosaic, with row letters and column numbers as buttons for whole rows/columns. Above 200 sections the grid scrolls with sticky headers (checked with 294 sections).
- "Nur offene Abschnitte" appears once at least one section is fully laid.
- The range field is parsed exactly: "A1-B2" selects A1, A2, B1, B2; "Z99" or an unreadable entry is rejected with a message and changes nothing.

**Export in parts (new `src/core/pdfExportPlan.ts`)**
- Memory need is a guide value (1 KB per coded stone, 0.1 KB uncoded, 5 KB per per-stone coordinate row, times 2), compared with 35 % of `performance.memory.jsHeapSizeLimit`, else 150 MB. I re-measured the constants against the current generator and they still hold.
- Over budget, the step offers "Teil k/N" for consecutive section runs, evenly sized, one download per click, with links kept for re-download. A section that alone exceeds the budget is explained with a link to step 9.
- "Trotzdem als eine Datei" stays available as a deliberate extra step, because the 150 MB fallback is conservative on desktop Firefox/Safari.

**Crash flag and safety**
- `mp.pdfInFlight` is written before each job and cleared after success, error, cancel and normal page unload. If it is still there on the next visit, a notice appears and the device's budget is halved (stored in `mp.pdfBudgetMb`, with a reset link).
- A stale computation disables export until "Mit alter Berechnung exportieren" is ticked, or the user follows "Jetzt neu berechnen".
- After a photo replace without recompute, the "Originalfoto" page is left out and the list says why.
- Saving is awaited and shown with `SaveResultNote`; "Abbrechen" ends the job; earlier object URLs are revoked.
- Exports now live in a small store (`pdfExportStore.ts`), so progress, cancel and finished files survive a step change.

All new text is in de/en/tr in `src/i18n/ext/w5-pdf-export-ui.ts`; it also overrides `pdfui.many`.
packages.notes:
**Deviations from the briefing, with reasons**

1. **The estimate is measured, not only planned.** `planPdfPages` without measured facts was far off for the current generator (portrait sample: 30 instead of 47, because cut lists and templates are unknown). I added a worker request `pdfPlan` that runs `pdfLayoutFacts` (the w4 dry run) with only the image dimensions; `planPdfPages` with those facts gives the page count of the PDF. Numbers still carry "ca." before export, as the rules require.

2. **Out-of-ownership edits to the worker (additive only).** `protocol.ts` gets one request and one response member, `compute.worker.ts` one new `case 'pdfPlan'` (the existing `pdf` case is untouched), `client.ts` one more channel name. I chose this over a separate worker file because that would bundle jsPDF and pdf.ts a second time (about 520 KB) and duplicate the font loader. w5-target-colours does not own these files.

3. **The picker is always a grid**, not chips up to 200 and a grid above. Cells keep the classes `btn chip primary` and the ID as their only text, so the w4-laying-workbench check for 'PDF B2' still passes.

4. **Coordinate mode select added now** (Kompakt / Je Stein). It was planned for w6, but without it the limit field had no effect in the only selectable mode, and the "Je Stein" page count is the 98-page case from the finding.

5. **Save result is shown in the step, not in the app-wide toast** (`announce:false`). In parts mode a toast per part would stack up. If the step is closed when the save finishes, the result is announced app-wide instead.

6. **"Trotzdem als eine Datei" and "Trotzdem versuchen" exist** as deliberate overrides. Without them desktop Firefox/Safari users would be blocked by the 150 MB fallback for exports that work today.

7. **Crash notice wording is "vermutlich zu groß"**, because a leftover flag can also come from an app killed in the background. The flag is cleared on `pagehide`, so a normal reload is not reported.

8. **Toggling templates off does not reduce the total by exactly the template pages**: the compact coordinate list grows (portrait: 8 → 13 pages) because it then marks templates as "nicht im PDF". The toggle hints therefore show that part's pages ("ca. 6 Seiten"), not a "+".

**Other out-of-ownership edits (both e2e, minimal)**
- `e2e/w2-android-platform.e2e.cjs`: the PDF check reads the path from the step's own note (`pdf-save-note`) instead of `save-toast`.
- `e2e/w3-pdf-foundations.e2e.cjs`: filling the coordinate limit is now conditional, since the field only exists for "Je Stein". Its assertions were already for the compact list.

**Not done / for later packages**
- After generation the step shows size and links, but not the real page count. That needs the worker to return pages (w6-pdf-finish, step 1).
- Part PDFs carry no "Teil k/N" in their headers yet; the UI marks this as "unvollständig" and puts the part number in the file name. For w6: `start()` in StepPdf already has `{index, total}` per part to pass into `pdfOptions`.
- Each part still prints all templates up to the limit (w6 restricts this to referenced ones).
- CSV export gating on stale state is in StepPlan, which this package does not own.
- Nothing was tried on a real Android device or in Firefox/Safari; the 150 MB fallback path is covered by unit tests only.
- For w7 (README): describe the measured page estimate, the section picker and range notation, export in parts with the guide values, the crash notice and budget reset, and the stale confirm.

**New files beyond the briefing's list:** `src/core/pdfExportPlan.ts`, `src/ui/project/pdfExportStore.ts`, `src/ui/project/pdfPlanFacts.ts`, `tests/w5-pdf-export-ui.test.ts`, `tests/w5-pdf-export-ui-store.test.ts`.
